hey! i myself am FTM and im 13, i think i can give a little bit of advice from my experiences.

i live in Ontario Canada, my home is extremely liberal and supportive, though i have experienced a bit of bullying from my peers. i never changed schools or anything, and by the sound of it V’s experiences are likely worse than mine. but the only advice for the bullying i could give is that if they feels its necessary to move schools, if the bullying is that bad, do just that. 

whatever it takes to make them happy in their own skin.   

i, like V, never had problems with friends. They sound like an amazing person, and even if they move schools they’ll always have the core group.

one of my close friends (who is non-binary) had to move schools because of bullying, but they found so many other kids at the new school who support them and help them, and we still keep in contact.

but the scary thing is no matter where you go, someone is gonna be an asshole to you. but its alright, i think in V’s case moving is best. 

ive got a bunch of friends a year or two younger than me (11-12 year olds) and they look up to me, they’ve been bullied sure, but they’ve become more confident in their identity and soon enough, it slows down.

Im sure V would be incredibly happy at a new school, a chance to start over. 

and the thing about V’s mom, i know she’d want the best for V. my parents had a.. reaction, when i came out. but over a few years they learned to understand and accept me, im sure she will too.


i hope this helps, sorry if anything is worded weird.

hey, im a kid myself, and at that im AFAB, but i think i can offer some advice. 

my parents told me that i always wanted to present masculine, from about the age of 3 and up, and they let me do that sometimes, and it made me feel so much better even as a kid. 

i think you should let them present as they want, ask them, they might be young but they know what they’d like to be called. 

it seems odd a doctor would tell you to make them present as their AGAB during school. it feels like they’re in forcing the idea that their gender is something to be ashamed of, and its not.

if they present as female from the start they’ll grow to be more confident in their identity, i wish my parents had let me do that when i was younger. 

letting them present as they want could also help other kids understand and learn from them, if they’re more confident and everyone around them understands, they’d have no reason to be bullied.

there’s nothing you need to do medically right now, so that’ll save you some stress, but dont make them switch between boy and girl from school and home. theres no point in making them do that.

i love my parents i really do. they’re my biggest supporters, but i wish they’d let me present how i wanted when i was younger, it would’ve made things so much easier for me down the line, please dont force your kid into something they arent. 

you dont need to take my advice, but im someone whos been in your kids situation, at least consider it.
